enhancement.definition: The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) is a statutory anti-corruption oversight body constituted under the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003. For this topic, the core study is the Commission's statutory constitution and its functions, powers, inquiry framework, reporting and accountability mechanisms under the Act.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: The CVC's authority is statutory, not an unrestricted supervisory power over every administrative decision. The Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003 structures the Commission's constitution and functions. Section 8 sets out important functions and powers, including superintendence over specified Delhi Special Police Establishment investigation functions, directions subject to statutory limits, inquiries/investigations on specified references or complaints, review of investigation progress and advice on matters referred to the Commission.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003 — sections 3–8, 8A–8B, 9–19 as applicable to constitution, appointments, service, removal, functions, proceedings, inquiries, annual reporting and miscellaneous powers. Section 8 is the principal statutory anchor for functions and powers.
essentialIngredients: Identify the statutory source: Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.
Identify the institutional provision governing the Commission's constitution and membership.
Identify the precise function or power invoked and its statutory trigger under section 8 or the applicable later provision.
Check whether the matter concerns the public servants, institutions, offence categories or references falling within the statutory scope.

Where the Commission exercises superintendence or gives directions concerning the Delhi Special Police Establishment, apply the statutory limitation that the Commission cannot require investigation or disposal of a particular case in a particular manner.
Separate the Commission's statutory role from the final adjudicatory or prosecutorial decision of another competent authority.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: The Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003 creates the statutory framework for the CVC. A good answer should first identify the relevant provision and then classify the challenged or proposed action as constitution, appointment, inquiry, investigation oversight, advice, reporting, or another statutory function. Section 8 is central to the functions-and-powers analysis. Its listed functions include specified superintendence over the Delhi Special Police Establishment, directions for the statutory responsibility entrusted to that establishment subject to the Act's limitation, inquiry or investigation on specified references or complaints, review of investigation progress, review of pending prosecution-sanction applications, and tendering advice on specified matters. The statutory limits matter: the Commission's oversight should not be converted into an assertion of power to dictate the result of an individual investigation. The answer should therefore identify the source of power, statutory trigger, affected institution/person, procedural stage, available review route and precise relief sought.

examples.title: Section 8 scope example
examples.body: A complaint alleges that a covered Central Government public servant committed an offence within the statutory field of the CVC Act. The first question is not whether the CVC is generally an anti-corruption body, but whether the complaint falls within the statutory category and whether the applicable inquiry/investigation function under section 8 is engaged.

examples.title: Superintendence limitation example
examples.body: The CVC reviews the progress of an investigation within its statutory field. That oversight does not by itself authorise the Commission to dictate that the investigating agency must investigate or dispose of the particular case in a specified manner. The statutory limitation must be addressed separately from the existence of supervisory power.

enhancement.problemApplication: A public servant challenges a CVC action arising from an anti-corruption complaint. Apply the sequence: (1) identify the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003 provision relied upon; (2) identify the statutory class of person/institution and offence or reference involved; (3) identify the procedural stage; (4) test whether the statutory trigger is satisfied; (5) distinguish permissible oversight/advice from an impermissible direction beyond the Act; and (6) identify the competent forum and precise relief.
keyTakeaways: The CVC's powers must be traced to the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.
Section 8 is the principal provision for functions and powers and must be read with its statutory limitations.
Do not equate administrative oversight with power to dictate the outcome of a particular investigation.
Always identify the statutory trigger, affected institution, procedural stage and exact relief.
